entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gentius was an Illyrian king belonging to the Labeatan dynasty, ruling from 181–168 BC. He was the son of Pleuratus III, who maintained positive relations with Rome.

Gentius's capital city was Scodra, now Shkodër, Albania, a strategic location along the Via Egnatia.

His reign saw the Illyrian kingdom's interactions with the Roman Republic, with Gentius himself becoming a vassal of Rome.

Despite the Roman influence, Gentius's dynasty continued to maintain its Illyrian identity.

This legacy of Illyrian autonomy would be remembered by later generations.

Gentius's story serves as a microcosm of the complex relationships between ancient civilizations.
